upstream.tag_qualification: The official v1.7.12 ref resolves directly to the commit object; no annotated tag object exists to vendor.
upstream.subject: Merge pull request #355 from DaveGamble/release-1.7.12

commit_signature.qualification: The official commit carries a GitHub web-flow signature, but this compact snapshot does not vendor a trust root; only Git object integrity is claimed.

selection.classification: authenticated public tagged compatibility baseline for the stock linked parse-side cJSON implementation; production-excluded
selection.lower_discriminator: get_object_item (0x004D8354) carries both the case-sensitive loop guard and the final NULL-string gate of upstream issue #315, shipped in v1.7.9; v1.7.8 has neither.
selection.upper_discriminator_1: buffer_skip_whitespace (0x004D7E1E) lacks the v1.7.13 cannot_access_at_index exhausted-buffer early return (#358).
selection.upper_discriminator_2: parse_array (0x004D80D8) and parse_object (0x004D81CC) lack the v1.7.14 head->prev tail store (#503).
selection.upper_discriminator_3: parse_number (0x004D7A5C) uses the pre-v1.7.19 64-byte stack number buffer, not the v1.7.19 allocated temporary (#939).
selection.linked_function_identity: All 21 linked parse-side functions are byte-identical C text between v1.7.9 and v1.7.12 (re-verified function-for-function during snapshot admission); the whole-file diff between those tags is confined to the dead-stripped print/create/edit/utils side.
selection.compatibility_qualification: v1.7.12 is the reproducible tagged baseline at the ceiling of the proven interval, not a claim about the private Even checkout, vendoring path, or exact historical tag. No Even modification of the linked functions was found; the binary is consistent with an unmodified upstream build with ENABLE_LOCALES=Off.

snapshot.scope: The three pristine upstream files that cover the linked parse-side closure: cJSON.c, cJSON.h, and the MIT LICENSE at v1.7.12

g2_boundary.production_decision: explicitly production-excluded at admission: the 2,572 stock body bytes remain cut-forward. Production admission requires a compiler/ABI readiness matrix against the authenticated baseline, reviewed overlay integration, and ownership accounting; identification and vendoring are not admission.
